verified.entry_point: library API: Client::getDatabase / Client::getCollection / Database::getCollection and the public MongoDB\Operation constructors; refused with MongoDB\Exception\InvalidArgumentException before any server call
routes: period in a database name (leading, trailing, several)
NUL byte in a database name
NUL byte in a collection name
period inside a collection name / namespace (must be preserved)
bulk-write namespace assembled from a name pair
collection handle resolved from a namespace
verified.services: none at run time (no mongod; all tests are constructor/API-level and offline, like the project's own regression tests for this advisory)
verified.project_tests_run: vendor/bin/phpunit tests/Operation/{Find,InsertOne,InsertMany,Update,Delete,BulkWrite,RenameCollection}Test.php — 547 tests pass at the pinned commit and with the reference fix
verified.build: php:8.3-cli-bookworm + PECL mongodb 2.5.5 + composer install (offline at test time)
verified.local_checks: all 56 security tests fail on the injected pinned tree and pass on the oracle; all 17 functional tests pass on both; every checks/ patch behaves as declared in local PHPUnit runs

wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the sink consumes the two names directly; there is no proxy or neighbouring resource to authorise in their place
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: the library has no role, secret or authority lookup; a name is judged on its own content

traps.shape: a period is legitimate inside a collection name (GridFS fs.files/fs.chunks, dotted user collections); only the database part may reject it
traps.realistic_because: rejecting the delimiter in both names is the obvious symmetric fix; the project's own GridFS and dotted collections make it a breaking change

traps.shape: the lower-level public operation constructors take database and collection names directly and had no check at the pinned commit
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; the facade passes already-validated names, so the operation layer looks safe

traps.pattern: A far site / route where the check never existed
traps.shape: a rename builds two namespaces; the target database and collection names never pass through a handle constructor
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; the handle's own name is validated, and the target is easily read as just another command parameter

traps.shape: a client bulk write stores its namespace as a string; a name-taking variant builds the namespace itself and bypasses the validated handle path
traps.realistic_because: code a maintainer could plausibly have written next to withCollection; it is reachable through the public client bulk-write API

traps.pattern: B injected sibling (separator shape trap), main lever
traps.shape: a namespace is split with an unbounded explode, so a period inside the collection part silently retargets the handle to a shorter collection name
traps.realistic_because: code a maintainer could plausibly have written next to getNamespace(); a namespace looks like 'db.coll', and the collection part may legitimately contain periods
